title: Machine learning identifies disordered twist-angle sequences with strongly reduced thermal conductivity in multilayer graphene
summary: Bayesian optimization and a CNN, coupled to non-equilibrium molecular dynamics, selected two-angle disordered twisted multilayer graphene structures with substantially lower simulated cross-plane thermal conductivity than aligned and periodic stacks. The optimized 14-layer sequence reached 0.095 W m−1 K−1 versus 0.512 W m−1 K−1 in aligned graphene in the reported model; phonon participation ratios and dynamical structure factors support strong partial phonon localization.
ai_technology: Bayesian optimization (COMBO) and convolutional neural network coupled to molecular-dynamics simulations

evidence.tested: Bayesian optimization and a CNN, coupled to non-equilibrium molecular dynamics, selected two-angle disordered twisted multilayer graphene structures with substantially lower simulated cross-plane thermal conductivity than aligned and periodic stacks.
evidence.unknown: This is a computational prediction supported by molecular-dynamics calculations, not a measured thermal-conductivity result from fabricated multilayer samples. The paper reports 80% reduction relative to aligned graphene for an optimized sequence and interprets phonon participation/structure-factor analyses as evidence of partial localization.
evidence.ai_role: Bayesian optimization selected low-conductivity twist sequences; the CNN screened the larger configuration space and proposed low-conductivity structures for subsequent molecular-dynamics evaluation.
